source_detail: Average Effective Tariff Rate — Policy through October 14, 2026 (Pre-Substitution)
title: Average Effective Tariff Rate
subtitle: Policy through October 14, 2026, Pre-Substitution
latest_source: Yale Budget Lab State of U.S. Tariffs (current statutory rate 11.0%, projected 11.8% by year-end)
methodology: Each data point is the headline overall pre-substitution average effective US tariff rate produced by the Yale Budget Lab Tariff Rate Tracker. Methodology: Yale applies announced tariff schedules (MFN + Section 232 + Section 301) at the HTS10 × trading-partner level to ~240 partners and ~20,000 HS10 product codes, weighted by pre-tariff import shares. Stacking rules: MFN is additive in all branches, Section 232 took precedence over IEEPA while IEEPA was in effect, Section 301 is always cumulative. Pre-substitution means the rate applies announced schedules to the pre-tariff import mix without adjusting for consumer/supplier behavioral substitution. Source pipeline: Budget-Lab-Yale/tariff-rate-tracker on GitHub.

notes: Each point through April 8, 2026 is the headline overall pre-substitution 'average effective US tariff rate' reported by the Yale Budget Lab. Post-April 8 points use Yale's published statutory rate snapshots and policy-event adjustments. The August 24 figure (10.9%) is directly from Yale's analysis.

Yale methodology: announced tariff schedules (MFN, Section 232, Section 301) applied at the HTS10 × trading-partner level to ~240 partners and ~20,000 HS10 product codes, weighted by pre-tariff import shares. Pre-substitution: no adjustment for consumer/supplier behavioral shifting. Pipeline open-source at github.com/Budget-Lab-Yale/tariff-rate-tracker.

Key 2025 events: April 2 'Liberation Day' 10% universal baseline, April 9 revised reciprocal rates (peak ~28%), May 12 US-China 90-day pause, May 28 CIT ruling briefly vacating IEEPA, August 1 reciprocal tariffs effective, November agricultural exemptions.

Key 2026 events: Feb 20 SCOTUS vacates IEEPA (rate drops to 9.1%), Feb 24 Section 122 10% surcharge, April 2 Section 232 metals + pharma proclamation, May 7 CIT invalidates Section 122 (stayed June 11), July 15 Section 301 25% on Brazil, July 24 Section 122 expires / Section 301 forced-labor tariffs (10%/12.5% on ~60 economies) replace it, July 31 Section 232 pharma 100% on Annex III companies, Sep 29 pharma 100% on all remaining companies.

Current rate (Oct 14, 2026): 11.0% pre-substitution. Yale projects 11.8% by year-end under current law due to scheduled tariff increases. Legal challenge: 25 states sued Aug 3 to block Section 301 forced-labor tariffs.

Collected/realized rate (different metric): Penn Wharton Budget Model reports 6.7% as of July 2026, reflecting trade diversion and substitution effects. The ~4pp gap between Yale's statutory 11% and Wharton's collected 6.7% measures the economic distortion caused by tariffs (importers rerouting supply chains, consumers substituting products).
